hints: A match starts wherever the pattern appears as a contiguous substring of the text.
The KMP prefix function tells how much of the pattern can be retained after a mismatch.
Scan text once, falling back through prefix links instead of restarting at each position.
analogy: When a character fails to match, reuse the longest pattern prefix that still matches the text suffix.
example: Pattern 'aba' occurs twice in text 'ababa', starting at positions 1 and 3.
algorithm: Compute the prefix-function for the pattern. Scan text with matched length j, fall back while characters differ, advance on match, count and reset to pi[j-1] after each full match.
correctness: KMP's fallback preserves exactly the longest viable prefix, so each occurrence is found and no possible start is skipped.
